solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spoke of dark follower of monarch?

indicators.note: we are told what is said, not written: the word spoken for 'dark' is the one to hear

parts.note: dark = night-time; the answer is spelt differently but said the same

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a shadowy henchman who trails after a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of KNIGHT is silent, so it and NIGHT are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight serves the monarch, and in chess stands just beside the king and queen.

clue.text: Packing container is suggested for venomous snake

indicators.note: the crate is only suggested by the sound of the answer, not spelt out in it

parts.note: a crate is a packing container; the snake's name is said the same way

explanation.surface: A shipping crate hints that a deadly snake is hiding inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling gives nothing away: only saying CRATE out loud leads to the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The krait is a highly venomous snake of South and South-East Asia.

clue.text: Reserve rearranged date for drink

parts.note: ice = reserve, a cold formality of manner

indicators.note: the letters of 'date' are put in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone rebooks a date to go for a drink instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a booking, which fits the date; here it is the noun, a chilly aloofness, which is ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: tea served chilled over ice is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Stolen jacket — a tricky case

parts.note: hot = stolen, as in hot goods
a jacket is a potato baked in its skin, a jacket potato

explanation.surface: A stolen coat turns into a difficult criminal case.
explanation.walkthrough: The jacket is not clothing: in Britain a baked potato is a jacket potato, so 'jacket' alone can stand for POTATO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an awkward issue no one wants to hold, a tricky case.

clue.text: Everyone's favourite outside platform

indicators.note: the favourite sits outside, wrapped round everyone

parts.note: the teacher's pet is the favourite
all = everyone

explanation.surface: The crowd's favourite speaker stands outside on a platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platform' tempts as a stage for a favourite performer; it is the definition. The ’s on 'Everyone’s' is only there for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallet is the flat wooden platform goods are stacked on for a forklift.

clue.text: Imitation table linen with no name

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, and it is taken away

parts.note: NAPERY, household table linen, loses its N

explanation.surface: A cheap copy of a tablecloth is sold without a brand name.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPERY is an old word for table linen such as napkins and tablecloths; take off N for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Apery is aping, the act of mimicking or imitating.

clue.text: Alfalfa from Swiss lake

definitions.meaning: a clover-like fodder plant, which in Britain goes by another name
the lake in central Switzerland named after the city on its shore

explanation.walkthrough: Lucerne is the usual British name for the fodder crop Americans call alfalfa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Lucerne is in central Switzerland, and lucerne is another name for alfalfa.

clue.text: Most gentle incline with replanted trees

parts.note: to tend (to) = to incline (to)

indicators.note: the trees are dug up and put back in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about the gentlest slope, planted anew with trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incline' reads as a slope, which suits the trees, but here it is the verb: to incline is to TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the superlative: tender and gentle both describe a soft touch, and 'most' matches the -EST ending.

clue.text: Range of colour allowed in crown

indicators.note: 'allowed' goes in the crown

parts.note: the pate is the crown of the head
let = allowed

explanation.surface: Rules on which colours may be used in a royal crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests royalty, but it is the top of the head, the PATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the range of colours an artist or design uses.

clue.text: Drop of French perfume

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
scent = perfume

explanation.surface: A single drop of French perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' reads as a dab of perfume; it is the definition, a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean a fall from higher to lower, as in a steep drop in a road.

clue.text: Crumpled jeans made him a cinematic heart-throb

indicators.note: crumpled jeans are twisted out of shape, as the letters are

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A rumpled pair of jeans made a film star's rebel image.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: denim was part of the rebel look he wore on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: James Dean, star of Rebel Without a Cause, was a 1950s screen heart-throb.

clue.text: Not moving position by a railway

parts.note: one's station is one's position
kept as it is
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A train stands still at a spot beside the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a railway station, and STATION is indeed there, but as 'position'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary means standing still, not moving.

clue.text: Does, say, return to grass

indicators.note: the word comes back the way it went

parts.note: does are female deer, examples ('say') of DEER

explanation.surface: Female deer go back to the meadow to graze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb; it is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass that grows in water.

clue.text: Meghan attracted in part to African country

indicators.note: only part of the words is wanted

parts.note: meGHAN Attracted

explanation.surface: The Duchess of Sussex found herself drawn in part to an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside Meghan and takes the A that opens 'attracted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one particular nation on the West African coast.

clue.text: German looking angry, scowling

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
to lower (rhymes with 'flower') is to frown or look sullen

explanation.surface: A German stands with an angry, scowling face.
explanation.walkthrough: LOWERING here is not letting down: the verb lour or lower means to frown, as a dark sky does.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a face set in an angry, sullen frown.

clue.text: Middle of Test ground is to be avoided

indicators.note: only the central letters of 'Test' are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of tESt
ground (between the teeth) = chewed

explanation.surface: A warning that the centre of a Test match pitch must not be walked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' is the cricket ground of a Test match in the surface; in the wordplay it is the past of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to shun, so eschewed means avoided.

clue.text: Mince pie consumed by awfully decent creature

indicators.note: the pie is eaten, taken inside the other word
mincing chops the pie into pieces, as the letters are

parts.note: anagram fodder, the outside

indicators.note: 'decent' is put awfully, badly out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, the inside

explanation.surface: A mince pie is eaten by a creature that is terribly well-mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pie' reads as one Christmas treat, but 'Mince' is an instruction acting on 'pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the many-legged arthropod is one kind of creature, a deliberately vague word.

clue.text: Preface spoken in Bow?

parts.note: the bow of a ship is its fore part
what is spoken is a word

explanation.surface: An introduction delivered in Bow, in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B dresses the ship's bow as Bow, the Cockney district of London; a word said in the fore is a FORE WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreword is a preface, the short piece before a book begins.

clue.text: The last link in the chain!

definitions.text: The last link in the chain!

parts.note: the surface points at the final ring of a metal chain
the setter means a supply chain, running from maker to shop to the person who finally uses the goods

explanation.walkthrough: The chain is a supply chain, not a metal one; the person at its far end is the one who finally uses the product.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the final consumer, the last link in the supply chain.

clue.text: Close outlet finally after sunset

parts.note: nigh = close, near

indicators.note: only the final letter of 'outlet' is kept

parts.note: the last letter of outleT

explanation.surface: A shop is told to shut after the sun has set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like the verb to shut, which suits the outlet; it is the adjective, near, which is NIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is adverbial: 'at night' and 'after sunset' mean the same time, so it stands in for the answer.

clue.text: Italian birds — number caged

indicators.note: the number is shut inside the birds

parts.note: geese are birds
NO is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Several Italian birds are kept in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' is the definition here, not a description of the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoese means of Genoa, the Italian port, or a person from there.

clue.text: Examine and register

definitions.meaning: to look over a document closely
what a meter or gauge does when it shows a figure

explanation.walkthrough: Both are verbs: you read (examine) a document, and a meter reads (registers) a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To read is to look over or study; an instrument reads when it registers a measurement.

clue.text: A tiny store ordered writing supplies

indicators.note: the letters are put in order, arranged anew

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A small shop has put in an order for pens and paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as buying stock, which suits the store; it is the instruction to rearrange. Compare 11 across, STATIONARY with an A.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery is paper, envelopes and pens, writing supplies.

clue.text: Baseless Japanese martial arts instructor's opinion

indicators.note: in a down answer the base is the bottom letter, and it is removed

parts.note: SENSEI, a martial arts teacher, loses its last letter I

explanation.surface: A karate master's view is dismissed as groundless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baseless' looks like a verdict on the opinion; it is an instruction to drop the letter at the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense can mean an opinion or view, as in 'the sense of the meeting'.

clue.text: Heavy drinker gets up to transfer plants

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading bottom to top

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drunk rises to move the pot plants around.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPER is an old word for a drunkard; read upwards it becomes REPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot is to move a plant into a new pot.

clue.text: Protest from Democrat is posted

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
kept as it is
posted = sent by mail

explanation.surface: A Democrat's objection has been mailed or put online.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a news line; the wordplay is three plain pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean open disagreement with those in charge.

clue.text: Confirmation of right to hold gun overturned

indicators.note: the right holds the gun inside it

parts.note: RT is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: the gun is turned over, reading backwards

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A court confirms the right to bear arms has been struck down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to hold gun' reads as the right to bear arms; in the wordplay RT is the holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is written confirmation that something was paid or received.

clue.text: Collect from heartless horticulturalist

indicators.note: the heart of the word, its middle letters, is taken out

parts.note: GARDENER loses its middle two letters, DE

explanation.surface: Someone takes a harvest from a cold-hearted gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: GARDENER has eight letters, so its heart is the central pair DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to gather in, and the answer first meant storing grain.

clue.text: Poor Teresa put in another chair

indicators.note: the name is in poor shape, its letters out of place

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Unlucky Teresa has been moved to a different seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like sympathy for Teresa; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition spells out the word's parts: RE- is 'again' or 'anew', and to seat is to put in a chair.
